questions.stem: India's PINAKA Multi-Barrel Rocket Launcher system, developed by DRDO, saw its first operational combat deployment during which conflict?

options.option_text: Operation Pawan (1987–90) in Sri Lanka against LTTE militant positions
Kargil War (1999), providing long-range saturation rocket fire support
Bangladesh Liberation War (1971) along the eastern theatre front
Operation Meghdoot (1984) to secure positions on Siachen Glacier

questions.explanation: PINAKA was inducted into the Indian Army in 1999 and first saw active combat during the Kargil War, providing long-range artillery rocket support. Operation Pawan (IPKF in Sri Lanka) predated PINAKA's induction; it was not deployed there.

questions.stem: India's indigenously developed AKASH surface-to-air missile system has an operational engagement range of approximately:

options.option_text: 5–8 km, suited for very short-range point-defence roles only
25–30 km, designed to cover medium-range aerial threat zones
70–80 km, comparable to the advanced Akash-NG next-generation variant
120–150 km, classified under long-range strategic air-defence category

questions.explanation: The original Akash missile has a range of approximately 25–30 km, classifying it as a medium-range SAM. Option C (70–80 km) is a common trap referring to the Akash-NG (Next Generation) variant, not the fielded Akash system.

questions.stem: The BRAHMOS supersonic cruise missile achieves speeds above Mach 2.8 primarily because of which propulsion configuration?

options.option_text: Single-stage turbojet with variable inlet geometry for sustained high speed
Two-stage system: solid-propellant rocket booster plus ramjet sustainer engine
Scramjet engine that ignites autonomously once the missile crosses Mach 2.5
Dual liquid-propellant stages with afterburner activated at terminal approach

questions.explanation: BrahMos uses a two-stage propulsion: a solid rocket booster accelerates it to ramjet ignition speed, then the ramjet sustains supersonic cruise. Option C (scramjet) is wrong — scramjets operate at hypersonic speeds (Mach 5+), which BrahMos does not reach; Option A (turbojet) is typical of subsonic cruise missiles like Tomahawk.

questions.stem: India's NAG anti-tank guided missile enables 'fire-and-forget' capability through which terminal guidance mechanism?

options.option_text: Semi-active laser homing, requiring the operator to lase the target continuously
Wire-guided command to line-of-sight, controlled by joystick after launch
Imaging Infrared (IIR) seeker that autonomously locks onto a tank's heat signature
Millimetre-wave active radar seeker that tracks the hull of armoured vehicles

questions.explanation: Nag uses an Imaging Infrared (IIR) seeker, allowing the operator to lock on and disengage — true fire-and-forget. Option A (semi-active laser homing) requires continuous designation after launch, which is not fire-and-forget. Option B (wire-guided) describes older-generation ATGMs like Milan.

questions.stem: India's nuclear doctrine references a 'NUCLEAR TRIAD'. Which of the following correctly defines this term in the Indian strategic context?

options.option_text: Three independent warhead designs: pure fission, boosted-fission, thermonuclear
Three delivery platforms: land-based missiles, aircraft-delivered bombs, submarine SLBMs
Three command levels: political authority, Strategic Forces Command, field commanders
Three range tiers: short-range tactical, medium-range theatre, intercontinental ballistic

questions.explanation: Nuclear Triad means the ability to deliver nuclear weapons via three independent platforms — land (Agni series), air (Mirage 2000/Rafale capable), and sea (INS Arihant with K-15/K-4 SLBMs). This ensures second-strike survivability. Option D confuses triad with range classification.

questions.stem: In September 2020, DRDO successfully demonstrated the Hypersonic Technology Demonstrator Vehicle (HSTDV) using scramjet propulsion. Approximately what Mach number did the vehicle achieve during the test?

options.option_text: Mach 3.5, just above the conventional supersonic cruise missile threshold
Mach 6, confirmed hypersonic flight using the indigenous scramjet engine
Mach 8, comparable to China's DF-17 hypersonic glide vehicle peak speed
Mach 10, matching the reported top speed of Russia's Avangard glide vehicle

questions.explanation: The HSTDV test on 7 September 2020 achieved approximately Mach 6 at an altitude of ~30 km, validating DRDO's scramjet combustion technology. Option A (Mach 3.5) is subsonic relative to hypersonic definition (Mach 5+). Option C/D are speeds of foreign systems and significantly overstate what was demonstrated.

questions.stem: The 'AGNI-P' (Agni Prime) ballistic missile, successfully tested in 2021, introduced canisterisation to India's Agni programme. What is the primary operational advantage this provides?

options.option_text: Doubles warhead yield by confining propellant gases during boost-phase combustion
Enables rapid road-mobile launch readiness and concealed pre-deployment posture
Shields onboard missile electronics from electromagnetic pulse attack scenarios
Permits dual-warhead stacking within a single re-entry vehicle configuration

questions.explanation: Canisterisation seals the missile in a launch tube filled with inert gas, eliminating pre-launch fuelling delays and allowing covert road-mobile deployment — dramatically improving survivability and launch readiness. Option C (EMP shielding) is a separate hardening measure unrelated to canisterisation. Option A conflates canister pressure with warhead yield, which is incorrect.
